title: Exploring roles of the chitinase ChiC in modulating Pseudomonas aeruginosa virulence phenotypes
projectDescription: Chitinases are ubiquitous enzymes involved in biomass degradation and chitin turnover in nature. Pseudomonas aeruginosa (PA), an opportunistic human pathogen, expresses ChiC, a secreted glycoside hydrolase 18 (GH18) family chitinase. Despite speculation about ChiC's role in PA disease pathogenesis, there is scant evidence supporting this hypothesis. Since PA cannot catabolize chitin, we investigated the potential function(s) of ChiC in PA pathophysiology
sampleProcessingProtocol: Proteins were precipitated using chloroform and methanol, by the protocol described by Wessel and Flügge (1984). Following precipitation, the proteins were separated by SDS-PAGE with a 10% Mini-PROTEAN gel and then stained with Imperial Protein Stain. The gel was cut into several slices, after which proteins were reduced, alkylated, and in-gel digested. The peptides were cleaned and desalted using StageTips. The peptide samples were analyzed by a nano UPLC (nanoElute, Bruker) coupled to a trapped ion mobility spectrometry and a quadrupole time of flight mass spectrometer (timsTOF Pro, Bruker)
dataProcessingProtocol: MS raw files were processed with the MaxQuant software suite (version 2.2.0.0) for label-free quantification using 'match between runs. The proteins were matched against the UniProt proteome: UP000000653. The data was filtered to 1% FDR. Perseus (2.0.7.0) was used to analyze the data.
